name: Simone de Beauvoir
worldviewSummary: Beauvoir develops an existentialist ethics in which freedom is realized only by willing the freedom of others, and she shows how women have been constituted as the 'Other' relative to men. Femininity is not a natural destiny but a situation produced by history, upbringing and institutions.
biography: French philosopher, novelist and essayist. Her two-volume The Second Sex (1949) became a founding text of modern feminism; she also wrote The Ethics of Ambiguity (1947) and the Goncourt-winning novel The Mandarins.

concepts.description: Humanity is defined as male, and woman is defined relative to him as the inessential Other.

concepts.concept: One is not born a woman
concepts.description: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman: femininity is produced by civilization, not by biological, psychological or economic fate.
Humans are both free subjects and objects among things; ethics means assuming this ambiguity rather than fleeing it.

positions.statement: To will oneself free is also to will others free; one's freedom cannot be achieved through the oppression of others.
Biological facts do not by themselves establish a fixed hierarchy of the sexes; they take on meaning only within a social and economic context.
Paid work and economic independence are central conditions for women's liberation, though not sufficient by themselves.
positions.locator: Volume II, Part Four, 'The Independent Woman'

relations.note: The Second Sex criticizes psychoanalytic accounts of femininity.
